arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Richardson argued the core issue is whether Congress banned peer grading.
Mr. Kneedler stated FERPA regulates records maintained by institutions, not classwork.
Mr. Wright cited Senator Buckley's 1974 statement about teacher consent.
Mr. Wright noted the principal admitted students cheat when exchanging papers.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act. The law protects student education records. The dispute centers on whether peer grading creates such records.
